cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Holiday – a day of festivity or recreation when no work is done.

p.em: Example: I love to go to the beach during my summer holiday.

cosy-blockquote.p: Travel – make a journey, typically of some length.

p.em: Example: Many people like to travel to different countries by plane.

cosy-blockquote.p: Short ≠ Long – measuring a small distance or duration ≠ measuring a great distance or duration.

p.em: Example: A short weekend trip is very fun, but a long summer trip is more relaxing.

cosy-blockquote.p: Vacation – an extended period of recreation, especially one spent away from home or in traveling.

p.em: Example: We planned a winter vacation to go skiing in the mountains.

cosy-blockquote.p: Relax – make or become less tense or anxious.

p.em: Example: A warm bath helps me relax after a long day at school.

cosy-blockquote.p: Destination – the place to which someone or something is going or being sent.

p.em: Example: Paris is a very popular tourist destination for people from all over the world.

cosy-blockquote.p: Plan – a detailed proposal for doing or achieving something.

p.em: Example: Do you have a clear plan for your next weekend trip?

cosy-blockquote.p: Pack – fill a suitcase or bag with clothes and other items needed for travel.

p.em: Example: I need to pack my swimsuit and sunglasses for the beach trip.

cosy-blockquote.p: Active ≠ Passive – engaging or ready to engage in physically energetic pursuits ≠ accepting or allowing what happens or what others do, without active response or resistance.

p.em: Example: I prefer an active holiday with hiking and swimming rather than a passive one spent sitting in a hotel.

cosy-blockquote.p: Choose – pick out or select someone or something as being the best in a situation.

p.em: Example: It is always difficult to choose between a mountain holiday and a seaside holiday.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
A: A short holiday is great because you do not leave work. B: A long holiday lets you forget about work completely.
★ How often do you take a short holiday to rest?

A: It is exciting to travel to a nearby town for a weekend. B: It is better to travel to a far country for a month.
★ Do you like to travel by train or by plane?

A: A short trip is easy to organize and very cheap. B: A long trip gives you more time to see everything.
★ Do you prefer a short weekend trip or a long summer trip?

A: A short vacation every month keeps you very happy. B: A long summer vacation is the best way to rest.
★ What is your favorite season to take a vacation?

A: You can relax very well during a quick three-day weekend. B: You need two weeks to truly relax and feel happy.
★ How do you usually relax after a busy day?

A: Visiting a quiet destination nearby is very peaceful. B: An exotic, far-away destination offers a much bigger adventure.
★ What is the most beautiful destination you have ever visited?

A: It is simple to plan a quick weekend trip. B: You must plan a long trip very carefully.
★ Do you like to plan every detail of your trip?

A: You only need to pack a small bag for a weekend. B: You have to pack a big suitcase with clothes.
★ Is it hard for you to pack your bags?

A: A short trip keeps you active because you move fast. B: A long trip lets you stay lazy on the beach.
★ Do you prefer an active holiday or a lazy one?

A: It is fun to choose a different town every month. B: It is better to choose one place for a month.
★ How do you choose your travel destinations?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
A: A short holiday is too fast, and you cannot rest. B: A long holiday is very expensive and hard to pay.
★ Have you ever felt tired after a short holiday?

A: Spontaneous travel can be very stressful for new tourists. B: Long-distance travel causes bad tiredness and jet lag.
★ Does long-distance travel make you feel tired?

A: A short trip is too fast to learn any culture. B: A long trip can make you feel very homesick.
★ Do you think a short trip is too fast?

A: A short vacation feels like a waste of packing time. B: An excessively long vacation can make you feel bored.
★ Have you ever felt bored during a long vacation?

A: It is impossible to relax when checking your watch. B: You cannot relax if you worry about your home.
★ Is it easy for you to relax?

A: A nearby destination can feel too similar to home. B: A far destination is hard if you do not speak.
★ Would you visit a destination if it had no internet?

A: Traveling without a plan can lead to bad hotels. B: A strict plan ruins the fun of surprising ideas.
★ Have you ever traveled without any plan?

A: If you do not pack well, you lose your clothes. B: Lugging heavy bags that you had to pack is bad.
★ Do you usually pack too many things?

A: Being too active leaves you more tired than before. B: A long, non-active trip makes you lose physical health.
★ Do you feel tired when your holiday is active?

A: It is hard to choose a place with limited time. B: It is risky to choose one place if you hate it.
★ Is it hard for you to choose travel options?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am prefer long holidays. → Correct: I prefer long holidays. ((Verb conjugation check: do not use 'am' before simple active verbs.))
Incorrect: It was a very good trip. → Correct: It was a wonderful / fantastic trip. ((Style: use more expressive adjectives like 'wonderful' or 'fantastic'.))
Incorrect: I have been in France last year. → Correct: I went to France last year. ((Past simple is required with specific past time markers like 'last year'.))
Incorrect: I am looking forward to go on holiday. → Correct: I am looking forward to going on holiday. (('Look forward to' is followed by a gerund/noun, not an infinitive.))
